title: Spectrally Programmable Spin-Polarized Photocurrents in WSe$_2$-NiPS$_3$ Magnetic van der Waals Heterostructures
authors: Rajesh Kumar Yadav, Michal Poplinger, Adi Levi, Adi Harchol, Nirman Chakraborty, Thomas Brumme, Thomas Heine, Efrat Lifshitz, Doron Naveh
abstract: Efficient generation and control of spin-polarized currents in semiconductors remain central challenges for spin-based electronics, particularly due to impedance mismatch and the reliance on magnetic fields or ferromagnetic contacts. Here, we introduce a materials platform for spectrally programmable spin transport based on a van der Waals heterostructure combining the antiferromagnetic semiconductor NiPS$_3$ with WSe$_2$. In a p-n diode architecture, circularly polarized excitation produces pronounced photoconductive resonances with spin polarization reaching 80% near the Neel temperature and persisting at 30% at room temperature. Remarkably, selected spectral bands retain their polarization sign across the magnetic phase transition, evidencing robust, spectrally protected spin-polarized current generation. Polarization-resolved photogalvanic measurements reveal a dominant circular injection-current mechanism, confirming spin-polarized carrier transport. First-principles calculations show that an applied electric field induces interfacial hybridization and spin-layer locking, giving rise to localized symmetry breaking and enhanced optical absorption while preserving global time-reversal symmetry. These results establish spectral tuning of excitation as a new control knob for spin transport, enabling spin-current generation without magnetic fields or polarization switching. Our findings position magnetic van der Waals heterostructures as a versatile platform for opto-spintronic functionality and spectrally programmable spintronic devices.
summary: This work introduces a novel opto-spintronic platform using a $	ext{WSe}_2-	ext{NiPS}_3$ van der Waals heterostructure. By using circularly polarized light, the researchers generate highly spin-polarized photocurrents. Crucially, they show that the spin polarization remains robust across the material's magnetic phase transition, establishing spectral tuning as a powerful, field-free control mechanism for spin-current generation.
main_problem: The core challenge addressed is the efficient generation and control of spin-polarized currents in semiconductors, overcoming limitations like impedance mismatch and the need for external magnetic fields.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that spectral tuning of excitation light in a $	ext{WSe}_2-	ext{NiPS}_3$ van der Waals heterostructure can generate robust, spectrally protected spin-polarized photocurrents without external magnetic fields.
method: The study combines experimental measurements (photocurrent, photogalvanic spectroscopy using circularly polarized light) with first-principles electronic structure calculations.
model_or_system: The physical system is a p-n diode heterostructure composed of the antiferromagnetic semiconductor $	ext{NiPS}_3$ and the semiconductor $	ext{WSe}_2$. The mechanism relies on interfacial hybridization and spin-layer locking induced by an electric field.
key_observables: Photocurrent spectra ($	ext{I}$ vs. photon energy $\epsilon$), degree of photocurrent polarization ($\eta$), and the persistence of spin polarization across the magnetic phase transition.
important_parameters: Temperature (especially near the Néel temperature), excitation photon energy ($\epsilon$), and the applied electric field strength.
main_assumptions: The observed effects are attributed to electric-field-induced interfacial hybridization and symmetry breaking, which allows spectral tuning to control spin transport.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the diode, temperature-dependent photocurrent spectra showing circular dichroism, and the polarization dependence of the photogalvanic response as a function of polarization angle.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem, presents the $	ext{WSe}_2-	ext{NiPS}_3$ platform, details measurements showing high spin polarization, explains the mechanism via interfacial hybridization and symmetry protection, and concludes by positioning the material for opto-spintronic applications.
why_interesting: The concept of using spectral tuning as a control knob for spin transport is highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum optics, as it suggests a non-magnetic, purely optical method to manipulate spin states in solid-state devices.
